title: Embeddings hosting & rerank pathing — Pinegrove discovery
summary: Initial scoping call for Pinegrove's product search rerank pilot. Customer is evaluating where to run embeddings + reranker: Redwood hosted API for speed vs Dedicated pools for predictable throughput vs Private VPC/on-prem for compliance. Main constraints: 500 qps peak embed fanout, 150–250ms tail latency target for search, cost sensitivity at scale, and strict audit/KMS requirements. Agreed next step: run a 2-week throughput smoke test + Redwood to share SOC2/HSM/KMS docs and a draft pricing model for dedicated baseline.
action_items: Maya Chen (AE): Send pilot pricing baseline + dedicated commitment options by 2026-03-16
Luca Ortiz (SE): Prepare suggested model config (embed dims, quantization, batching) and initial test harness for 500 qps by 2026-03-18
Tom Briggs (Infra): Provide sample traffic profile (qps distribution, payload size) and current vector DB index stats by 2026-03-15
next_steps: Schedule infra deep-dive with Pinegrove infra (Luca + Tom) for benchmark plan (target week of 2026-03-22)
Redwood to share SOC2 and KMS/HSM integration doc links
Customer to grant read-only access to small slice of their vector DB for smoke benchmarks (credentials via secure channel)
Follow-up pricing + SLA email from AE within 4 business days
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-03-12 15:30 PT; Duration: 52m; Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Samir (CTO Pinegrove), Renee (Head of Search), Tom (Infra), Priya (PM)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros? I'm Maya, I'm the AE working with you.
[00:08] Samir Patel: Samir here, CTO at Pinegrove. Renee will lead the search side. We're trying to figure out embedding hosting and rerank.
[00:15] Renee Gomez: Hi. yes, thanks. we've got a big seasonal push Q3 so we need to decide soon.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Got it. Luca, do you want to give a 2 minute overview of Redwood's options?
[00:27] Luca Ortiz: Sure yeah. Redwood offers hosted API which is simplest — you hit our REST/SDK, we return embeddings or rerank outputs. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools that you control capacity on, lower noisy neighbor variance and predictable throughput. Private is VPC or on-prem where the control plane is isolated and you manage networking and keys. There are trade offs: cost vs latency predictability vs compliance.
[01:05] Tom Briggs: Quick q — for private, is data ever leaving our VPC? We need to keep logs internal.
[01:12] Luca Ortiz: For Private deployments, the control plane can be configured so telemetry/audit logs can be forwarded to your systems. Raw token payloads can be kept local; we can support KMS/HSM integrations. We'll share the SOC2 and KMS docs.
[01:28] Priya Nair: For context, our current search stack: ES + a Faiss-ish vector DB for rerank. The embed pipeline currently runs on a small fleet on nights and we do nightly reindex. We want realtime shopping queries to go through rerank with a low latency budget.
[01:47] Renee Gomez: Numbers: avg qps 120 steadily, but peaks at 500 during promos. 90% of queries should sub-100ms server time but tail 95/99 must hit under 250ms end-to-end. Cost budget is tight — anything over $X per 1000 queries is hard to justify.
[02:10] Luca Ortiz: Okay that's helpful. A few clarifying questions: is reranker a separate model call after initial recall? Are you embedding per query and doing a fanout to the vector DB?
[02:20] Renee Gomez: Yes: we do a 64–128 dimensional dense embed for recall, topK is 200, then a reranker neural model (around 2–3B param currently) scores topK and returns top results. The reranker is the heavier part.
[02:40] Samir Patel: and we want to know what short term move is: run everything hosted for speed of integration, or go dedicated for predictable tail — or private because of some PCI-like compliance in EU and third party payment partners.
[02:53] Maya Chen: Sounds like three axes: latency & tail, cost at 500 peak qps, and compliance. We typically recommend an iterative path: start with hosted for discovery/functional eval, then if you need predictable tail and better unit economics migrate to Dedicated pools, and Private is for when audit/KMS/residency needs force it. But let's talk specifics — embed dims, fanout, rerank placement — because those change the economics.
[03:20] Luca Ortiz: On embed dimensionality: you mentioned 64–128 dims. Lower dims mean smaller vector size and cheaper fanout but sometimes slightly lower recall. We can also do compact quantized embeddings — 8-bit or even sparse sketches depending on your retrieval tolerance. For rerank, model placement options are: 1) host reranker in Redwood hosted endpoints so we run the 2–3B model in our runtime, 2) run rerank in Dedicated reserved GPUs that you commit to, or 3) bring your reranker into a Private deployment. Each has perf/cost tradeoffs.
[04:05] Tom Briggs: If we run the reranker hosted, does traffic go to Redwood's infra and then back to us for results? Any PII concerns?
[04:12] Luca Ortiz: For hosted, request and response payloads traverse Redwood; we retain only telemetry per your retention policy, but we can configure no-retain and sign NDA. For Private, the runtime sits in your VPC so the data never traverses public infra. We also support customer-managed KMS so keys never leave your domain.
[04:35] Renee Gomez: Are there examples of customers doing hybrid — embeddings hosted, rerank private?
[04:40] Luca Ortiz: Yes, hybrid patterns are common: embeddings can be computed with low-cost hosted endpoints and stored in your vector DB; rerank, being the heavy model, is often pinned to Dedicated or Private to control cost and latency. Another pattern: host a small lightweight reranker in-hosted for non-critical paths and fall back to private/dedicated in high-load or sensitive routes.
[05:05] Samir Patel: Our ops team is concerned about peak tail latency when fanout hits 200. If we fanout 200 per query and then run rerank for topK 200, that's a lot of model invocations. How do you handle batching and cache?
[05:20] Luca Ortiz: Our runtime supports continuous batching and KV/prefix caching. For rerank we can batch scoring across candidates where applicable; also, if you have stable prefixes we can use KV cache. For vector DB fanout, embedding cost is linear in fanout size, but rerank costs depend on model size and sequence length. We can apply quantized kernels to reduce GPU footprint.
[05:45] Priya Nair: What's the expected throughput on Dedicated? say if we reserve N GPUs what QPS does that map to for a 3B rerank?
[05:54] Luca Ortiz: Ballpark numbers: a single A100-class node with optimized kernels for a 3B model, with batching and small sequence lengths, might do 50–120 qps depending on allowed latency. So to support 500 peak qps with a 200 topK rerank you'd likely need horizontal sharding and autoscaling policy; Dedicated pools let you reserve baseline to meet your 95/99 SLOs. We'll do a capacity plan once we see your traffic histograms.
[06:22] Tom Briggs: How about cost directionally — hosted per-call vs dedicated reserved pricing? We need a sense for ROI.
[06:28] Maya Chen: I can share a baseline pricing calc after this call. Hosted is usage-based and simple to try; Dedicated has a commit and then lower unit costs at scale and better tail predictability. For some customers, the commit pays off after X qps sustained — we'll show modeled breakeven points.
[06:46] Renee Gomez: What about quantized rerank models? We worry quality dropoff.
[06:50] Luca Ortiz: We have quantization profiles that keep near-original quality for many workloads — 4/8 bit strategies and mixed-precision where necessary. Redwood Optimize can recommend a model/quantization profile per prompt set and run evals to measure quality delta. Worth noting: for rerank smaller bit-widths sometimes change ranking slightly; we usually run A/B against your eval prompts before production rollout.
[07:20] Samir Patel: Security: we need SOC2 plus the ability for our auditors to see audit logs and key rotation proofs. Also EU data residency for a subset of traffic.
[07:31] Maya Chen: We are SOC2 compliant (we'll share the report), we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for private deployments, and control-plane regionalization for data residency. For hosted, we can pin model endpoints to a region and set data retention policies.
[07:52] Priya Nair: Operationally, if we start with hosted and then move to Dedicated, how disruptive is the switch?
[07:58] Luca Ortiz: We designed the API to be consistent across modes. Rolling from hosted to dedicated is mostly configuration/deploy: you pin the model version and routing policy. There may be a short warmup for KV caches and tokenization artifacts but no code changes usually. If you move to Private there is more infra work but same surface area in the API.
[08:25] Renee Gomez: For our pilot we'd like to validate three things: 1) accuracy delta for 64 vs 128 dims, 2) cost per query at 500 peak with topK 200 and rerank in both hosted/dedicated, 3) tail latency under realistic traffic.
[08:41] Maya Chen: Good OK. Proposed pilot: two-week smoke test. Redwood runs a synthetic replay harness against your vector DB slice and a small sample of live traffic. We'll run both 64 and 128 embedding profiles, test quantized embeddings, and evaluate rerank in hosted and in a temporary Dedicated pool to compare latency and unit cost. Does that sound aligned?
[09:06] Samir Patel: Yes. we'll need a secure way to give a subset of vector data — we can create a masked dataset. Tom will coordinate.
[09:12] Tom Briggs: I'll put together index stats and traffic histogram and a masked data dump to share securely. Questions about credentials: do you support ephemeral keys for benchmarks?
[09:22] Luca Ortiz: Yes, we can accept time-limited keys and S3 signed URLs for data ingestion. We'll not persist raw payloads if requested.
[09:30] Renee Gomez: One more — for rerank model versioning and rollouts, is canary supported?
[09:35] Luca Ortiz: Yes we support canary and A/B rollouts at the routing layer, with trace-level observability and automatic rollback on quality regressions. We can tie regressions to your eval set and alert.
[09:50] Priya Nair: Do you have any reference architecture or recommended configs for a retail company with our profile?
[09:56] Maya Chen: We'll share a reference playbook that includes embed dim suggestions, quantization profiles, Dedicated sizing heuristics, and a recommended fallback policy (hosted rerank fallback to a smaller model under load). I'll attach it to the follow-up.
[10:12] Samir Patel: Another ops detail — we run our vector DB across three regions for redundancy; how does Redwood handle multi-region routing?
[10:20] Luca Ortiz: Smart routing — we can route requests by region, latency, or cost. For private deployments, you can pin runtime pools per region. For hosted we have multi-region endpoints and automatic fallback. In your case we'd probably colocate rerank or dedicate pools in the same region as the DB shards to cut cross-region latencies.
[10:40] Renee Gomez: Regarding the rerank model size, you suggested 2–3B. Could we use a smaller 700M model as a cheaper middle-ground?
[10:48] Luca Ortiz: Definitely. Many customers run a two-tier rerank: a cheaper 700M model as a fast baseline and a 3B model for expensive or high-value queries. You can also do confidence-based routing — only escalate to 3B when needed. That saves cost and helps meet tail SLOs.
[11:15] Maya Chen: Great. any blocker for the pilot besides sharing data and traffic histograms?
[11:19] Tom Briggs: No, timeline wise we want results within three weeks to inform Q2 planning.
[11:24] Maya Chen: We'll aim to start the week of 2026-03-22 if Tom can share artifacts by March 15.
[11:30] Renee Gomez: On compliance, we'd like to see the SOC2 and a note on your KMS/HSM partners and rotation cadence.
[11:36] Maya Chen: Noted. we'll attach SOC2 and the KMS integration doc.
[11:40] Samir Patel: Another thought: what about caching candidate rerank scores to avoid re-scoring? We have repeated queries in user sessions.
[11:48] Luca Ortiz: We can do ephemeral scoring cache for repeated candidate sets and also incremental rerank for session-level context. That can reduce rerank invocations significantly. Worth modeling in the pilot.
[12:05] Priya Nair: For the pilot, can we A/B quantized vs full precision rerank and measure ranking drift?
[12:12] Luca Ortiz: Yes, Redwood Optimize will run evals and provide drift metrics tied to your labeled prompts. We'll surface per-prompt deltas and aggregate MRR/PD differences.
[12:30] Maya Chen: okay i'm going to quickly recap next steps and owners. Maya will send pilot pricing and reference playbook; Luca will scope the test harness and config; Tom will provide masked data and traffic hist histograms; Renee/Priya will prepare evaluation prompts and success criteria. Any additions?
[12:50] Samir Patel: Also include proposed SLA for Dedicated (uptime and latency targets) in the doc.
[12:57] Maya Chen: will do.
[13:00] -- brief cross talk and wrap up --
[13:20] Maya Chen: Thank you all. we'll follow up with calendar invite for infra deep-dive and share docs.

End of recording.
questions: What is the breakeven qps for dedicated vs hosted?
Can rerank be cached effectively for repeated session queries?
How accurate are 8-bit quantized rerank models for our ecom prompts?
closing_recap: Agreed run a 2-week smoke test targeted at the week of 2026-03-22, Redwood to supply SOC2/KMS docs and pricing, Pinegrove to share masked vector data and traffic histogram, and an infra deep-dive to define benchmark specifics.
